twitterTweet this page
Art & Design Technology
Art and Design at Auriol provides our children with the skills, concepts and knowledge necessary for them to express their responses to ideas and experiences in a visual or tactile form. It fires their imagination and is a fundamental means of personal expression.
Armed with skills, knowledge of materials and appreciation of different artists, children have the freedom to explore their own ideas. They produce art confidently with the knowledge that there is no right or wrong and that making mistakes is an important part of the creative process. By learning this way, they develop a resilient attitude, confidence in creativity and love of art, which they can carry through to secondary school and beyond.
Children are taught the basic principles of Design Technology: Design, Make, Test and Evaluate. They learn how to think independently, be resourceful, innovative and enterprising.
We look at the user, the purpose, functionality, innovation and authenticity with an emphasis on designing real products for real people and addressing real problems.
They learn to evaluate their work to ensure a better future outcome and to work collaboratively either in small groups or as a class. Throughout their time at Auriol, they will develop their creative, technical and practical expertise to enhance their understanding of structures and mechanical systems and to enable them to solve real and relevant problems.
For further information, please see progression map at the bottom of this page.
Subject Leader: Mrs Sassa & Miss B
We are proud to share our entries for the Young Artists’ Summer Show at the Royal Academy of Arts. This is an incredible opportunity for young people aged 4–18 across the UK to create and submit artwork that expresses their unique voice. We look forward to hearing the results in May, but we believe every one of these pieces is a winner. See below for some of our entries.

Music
At Auriol, our music curriculum aims to inspire a lifelong love and appreciation for music in our pupils. We believe that music is a powerful tool for self-expression, creativity, and emotional development. Through our music lessons, we strive to ignite a passion for music, nurture individual talents, and provide opportunities for every student to explore and enjoy various genres, instruments, and musical styles.
Our music curriculum takes a holistic approach to music, in which the individual strands of performing, listening, composing, the history of music and the inter-related dimensions of music are woven together to create engaging and enriching learning experiences. We aim for pupils to develop their musical abilities through singing, playing instruments, and composing as well as developing their performance skills within the school and wider community. We encourage students to take risks, experiment with different musical techniques, and develop their confidence as musicians.
For further information, please see our progression map.
Subject Leader: Mrs Smith

History
At Auriol, pupils gain a coherent and progressive knowledge & understanding of Britain’s past and that of the wider world, through investigating key time periods and major historical themes through a pedagogy of enquiry. The sequenced and interconnected curriculum builds new knowledge onto what has already been taught leading to a deeper understanding and a recognition that there are similarities, differences and connections between eras, ultimately inspiring pupils’ passion and curiosity to know more about the past.
For further information, please see our progression map below.

Geography
At Auriol Junior School, our geography curriculum is designed to nurture curiosity and exploration while building independence and resilience in our pupils. We aim to instil a thorough knowledge of continents and countries, exploring similarities and differences to foster an understanding of our varied and ever-changing planet. Through engaging activities such as fieldwork and computer mapping, we teach practical skills that will be invaluable in our pupils’ future education. Our goal is to inspire a genuine passion for geography, encouraging curiosity, critical thinking, and a lifelong respect for our wonderful world.
Subject Leader: Mrs Gilbertson

Modern Foreign Languages
Our French curriculum is crafted to ignite a love for language, nurture curiosity about the world, and foster effective communication. Through engaging lessons and cultural exploration, we aim to instil a passion for linguistic diversity while integrating real-world contexts. Emphasising resilience, our curriculum provides challenges, failures, and successes that contribute to personal growth, building confident and globally-minded learners.
Our French curriculum supports the holistic development of each child, focusing on building self-confidence, fostering a sense of identity, and nurturing a growth mindset. Through language learning, students not only expand their linguistic abilities but also develop essential life skills that will serve them well in the future.

Mathematics
Maths at Auriol is focused on securing basic number knowledge and skills to be able to move on to develop a deep and lasting understanding of more complex mathematical concepts and skills. Children need to explore and secure their basic number knowledge at the bottom of the climbing frame before they can venture higher up to master more challenging concepts.
We encourage children to build on their concrete, pictorial and abstract levels of understanding through the use of manipulatives and a range of formal written methods. Learning is meaningfully linked to the real world, encouraging exploration, critical thinking and problem-solving.
Fluency and accuracy in number are developed across the school through daily speedy maths, maths lessons, times table rockstars and flip learning which consolidates classroom learning. Our maths curriculum is progressive and interconnected, preparing our pupils to exceed their expectations and to meet the challenges of a changing world with confidence and resilience.
For further information on what topics are taught when, please see our year group maps and whole school progression map below.
Subject Leader: Mrs Allum & Miss Swift

Science
At Auriol Junior School, our progressive science curriculum equips the children with the essential knowledge and scientific skills required to understand the uses and implications of science, today and for the future. Sequential lessons build upon prior knowledge and provide a range of science enquiries that support the children to answer scientific questions and foster a deeper understanding about the world around them.
Our goal is to promote a passion for exploration, providing children with the knowledge and skills to apply science in practical settings. By engaging in hands-on experiences, we encourage curiosity surrounding different scientific concepts, which empowers our learners to think as a scientist.
For further information, please see our Science progression map below.

Computing
At Auriol Junior School, our main aim is to equip all pupils with essential skills and knowledge to navigate the ever-changing digital landscape. Our primary focus is on fostering a deep understanding of principles such as computer science, information technology and digital literacy, ensuring that students develop problem-solving abilities and computational thinking from the start of their online journey. We prioritise the cultivation of responsible and ethical online behaviour, emphasising the significance of positive digital relationships and cybersecurity. Our intent is to instil digital literacy as a skill to empower students to critically evaluate information and navigate the digital world safely. By providing a comprehensive computing education, we aspire to prepare our pupils to be confident, adaptable, resilient and well-rounded individuals who are ready for the opportunities and challenges of the future.
For further information, please see our progression map below.
Subject Leader: Mr Reece Moore

Religious Education
At Auriol Junior School, our Religious Education curriculum is an integral part of our broad and inclusive educational approach, designed to promote spiritual, moral, and cultural development. We encourage reflection on personal beliefs within a wider religious context, while emphasising tolerance, mutual respect and a deep understanding of diverse faiths. We celebrate the many different religions of our pupils through inviting them to share their own experiences with others in the school. Through these initiatives, we aim to equip students with the skills and attitudes needed to thrive as considerate, responsible and open-minded individuals in our diverse world.
For further information, please see our progression map at the bottom of this page.

PSHE
At Auriol Junior School, the Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) curriculum plays a pivotal role for nurturing well-rounded individuals. With a central focus on diversity, we instil in our students an awareness and respect for varied perspectives, backgrounds, and cultures. By addressing a range of topics such as culture, ethnicity, gender and abilities we create an inclusive learning environment. Additionally, our curriculum prepares students for future life by integrating practical life skills, critical thinking, and decision-making processes.
Through PSHE, we aim to equip our students with the knowledge and attitudes necessary to thrive in a diverse and ever-changing world fostering an appreciation for and understanding of others' points of view.
Please find further information in our progression map below.

Physical Education
At Auriol Junior School, our Physical Education (PE) program aims to develop competence, instil a lifelong passion for physical activities, and promote sustained physical activity. Through progressively structured lessons, we foster skills that enable students to excel in a diverse range of physical endeavours, encouraging not only physical well-being but also a commitment to an active lifestyle. Emphasising engagement in competitive sports and activities, our PE curriculum promotes teamwork, sportsmanship, and resilience. By setting ambitious goals, we cultivate confidence and the ability to learn from both successes and setbacks, preparing students for the challenges of the world beyond school.
Our commitment to leading healthy, active lives fits seamlessly with the overarching school intent, contributing to the holistic development of well-rounded individuals ready to make positive contributions to society through their understanding and embodiment of a healthy and active lifestyle.
For further information, please see our progression map below.
Subject Leader: Mr Shaw

Reading
At Auriol, we are passionate about reading and believe that the teaching of reading is integral to a child’s understanding and appreciation of the world around them. We believe that reading is the key to unlocking the entire curriculum and as such, we are committed to enabling our children to become confident, fluent and lifelong readers across all subjects. At the heart of our strategy is our drive to foster a love of reading, enriching children’s learning that immerse them in a wide variety of stories and texts to inspire, interest and excite.
We are committed to providing a broad and diverse range of texts, genres and authors from across the curriculum which are rich in vocabulary. Reading for pleasure is the cornerstone of our approach as we endeavour to evoke an atmosphere where reading opens the doorway to learning and exploring the world in which we live. Once our pupils have unlocked the key to reading, it is our intention that they will be able to apply their reading skills to access any subject in their secondary education and beyond.
Subject Leaders: Mrs Benjamin

Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome and thank you for visiting Auriol Junior School website. It is an honour to lead the school. Auriol Junior is a three-form entry junior school in Surrey with a deaf resource base. We are proud to be a part of the Bourne Education Trust and work collaboratively with other primary and secondary schools across the Trust. Our motto Challenge, Inspire, Prepare is not just a set of words; it is a guiding principle that shapes the culture of our school.
We work tirelessly to create an environment where children are continually supported and challenged, fostering growth and development. Our rich curriculum and high quality teaching sparks curiosity and a desire for further knowledge in each child. At our school, children are given a wide range of opportunities where they may experience success and setbacks, nurturing resilience and adaptability. Our dedicated staff guide and support children in understanding their emotions and feelings, fostering their social and emotional development.
I know we are biased but Auriol is a great school. Children are happy and achieve well. Thankfully, Ofsted agreed :-)
Here are some excerpts from our recent (June 2025) Ofsted inspection:
'This is a school that fosters a caring ethos. Consideration for others is very important here. Regularly, the school urges pupils to self-reflect on their own and others’ feelings. Pupils behave well'.
'Pupils enjoy school and are happy here. The school recognises pupils’ talents and supports them to follow their interests'.
'The school has high expectations for pupils and supports them to reach their potential relentlessly'.
'Pupils achieve exceptionally well here. This is reflected in the school’s published outcomes in 2024, which are well above the national average. The ambitious, well-organised curriculum includes a wide range of subjects, in line with the national curriculum'.
'The school prepares pupils for later life exceptionally well...the school supports pupils to embrace and persist with challenge..the school emboldens pupils to push beyond perceived boundaries'.
At Auriol, we view education as a shared endeavour involving not just our children, staff and local governing committee but also parents and the wider community. We are dedicated to working collaboratively, ensuring that every child receives the support and care they need to thrive academically and emotionally.
See what our current families think of our school. Auriol Junior School | Ofsted Parent View
We would love the opportunity to show you around. Please call the office to arrange a tour.

Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome and thank you for visiting Auriol Junior School website. It is an honour to lead the school. Auriol Junior is a three-form entry junior school in Surrey with a deaf resource base. We are proud to be a part of the Bourne Education Trust and work collaboratively with other primary and secondary schools across the Trust. Our motto Challenge, Inspire, Prepare is not just a set of words; it is a guiding principle that shapes the culture of our school.
We work tirelessly to create an environment where children are continually supported and challenged, fostering growth and development. Our rich curriculum and high quality teaching sparks curiosity and a desire for further knowledge in each child. At our school, children are given a wide range of opportunities where they may experience success and setbacks, nurturing resilience and adaptability. Our dedicated staff guide and support children in understanding their emotions and feelings, fostering their social and emotional development.
I know we are biased but Auriol is a great school. Children are happy and achieve well. Thankfully, Ofsted agreed :-)
Here are some excerpts from our recent (June 2025) Ofsted inspection:
'This is a school that fosters a caring ethos. Consideration for others is very important here. Regularly, the school urges pupils to self-reflect on their own and others’ feelings. Pupils behave well'.
'Pupils enjoy school and are happy here. The school recognises pupils’ talents and supports them to follow their interests'.
'The school has high expectations for pupils and supports them to reach their potential relentlessly'.
'Pupils achieve exceptionally well here. This is reflected in the school’s published outcomes in 2024, which are well above the national average. The ambitious, well-organised curriculum includes a wide range of subjects, in line with the national curriculum'.
'The school prepares pupils for later life exceptionally well...the school supports pupils to embrace and persist with challenge..the school emboldens pupils to push beyond perceived boundaries'.
At Auriol, we view education as a shared endeavour involving not just our children, staff and local governing committee but also parents and the wider community. We are dedicated to working collaboratively, ensuring that every child receives the support and care they need to thrive academically and emotionally.
See what our current families think of our school. Auriol Junior School | Ofsted Parent View
We would love the opportunity to show you around. Please call the office to arrange a tour.

pageCache.text:
Performing Arts
At Auriol Junior School, we believe in nurturing the diverse talents and passions that reside within our children. Fully embracing the performing arts not only provides opportunities for children to celebrate and showcase artistic skills, it helps create the school environment we are proud of!
Through our range of events, we foster teamwork, resilience and the confidence to face challenges head on. Through collaborative projects and group performances, children learn the importance of working together towards a common goal. Diversity is celebrated with the rich tapestry of of talents and backgrounds in our school and we ensure that every child, regardless of their background of experience, has the opportunity to participate and flourish.
Performing Arts
facebookShare this page on Facebook
twitterTweet this page
Spring Playhouse
Every year, children work hard to prepare for the spring playhouse performance, a dazzling show full of dancing, acting, singing, signing and musical talent! All children who participate in the show partake in a range of clubs (some open invite and others require audition), practising their act for months leading to the final showcase. We encourage all children to participate as this really is a magical experience with the opportunity to perform on stage at the local theatre in Epsom!
Performance Poetry Week
Every year, we host an exciting competition across the school. Each class enters a performance poem they have been working hard to perfect and we invite guest judges to select their final winner based on performance criteria! This event usually takes place in autumn and there is a national theme every year, so keep your eyes peeled for the updates in our school newsletter.
Year 6 End of Year Production
Our final opportunity for Auriol children, giving them the best send off before heading to their new schools. Children in Year 6 audition each year for a part in their final production and head off to the local theatre for one last time to showcase their talent. A production is carefully selected each year, ranging from pirate adventures to superheroes saving the day, from neanderthals exploring the world to the tales of William Shakespeare. What will the next production be...?
Summer Fair Performances
At our annual school fair, a range of performances are shared with our community. Gymnastics and dance routines wow our crowds and our school choir provide a beautiful ambience amongst the many fundraising events taking place on the day. Many of our children take part in externally provided clubs and these also have the opportunity to showcase their talents on this day.

Auriol Junior School and The Mead Infant and Nursery School Local Governing Committee
In September 2024, Local Governing Committees (LGCs) at both Auriol Junior School and The Mead Infant and Nursery School began working under an alternative structure for governance. It was agreed at trust level and by both LGCs that both schools will be adopting this approach to governance.
Therefore, Auriol Junior School and The Mead Infant and Nursery School operated with a single LGC from September 2024.
As the schools move forward, this LGC structure will support Governor succession planning and will aid in the recruitment of high calibre governors who can offer between them the range of skills and competences required to ensure that combined LGC is strategic and highly effective.
Both schools are very excited to work collaboratively and the opportunities this may bring.
Daniel Sims Tracy Creasey James Knights
Chair of Governors Head Teacher The Mead Head Teacher Auriol

pageCache.pageTitle: The Role of Governors - Auriol Junior School
pageCache.text:
The Role of Governors
Auriol Junior School is part of the Bourne Education Trust. ‘Transforming schools; changing lives’ – the aim of the Bourne Education Trust is to create a community of outstanding schools with the highest aspiration and dedication to achieving the best outcomes for all learners.
Governance plays a key role in shaping the strategic direction of the school and challenging the school leaders to ensure every child has the opportunity to achieve their personal best. The Bourne Education Trust delegates the majority of powers and responsibilities to Auriol Junior School Governors under the Scheme of Delegation.
Parent representatives on the Governing board are an important part of our school and home partnership. Not only are they directly aware of the results of school policy on our children and are easily accessible to you the parents, but they can bring a variety of skills needed in the present day governing of schools.
Who are we? What do we do?
We are all volunteers who are either parents, live in the local community or are passionate about enabling your children to have the best education they can have, to be the best they can be. We have no statutory responsibilities however the Bourne Education Trust believes it’s important to have local voices to challenge and support the school. There are three parts to our job. 1. To work with the leadership team to set the strategic direction of the school 2. To hold the school and Trust to account for performance 3. To ensure the money is well spent and resources well used.
When do Governors meet? What do we talk about in meetings?
Local Governing Committee (LGC) meetings are held six times a year, once every half term. We talk about things that help us hold the school to account, for example the headteachers report and safeguarding. We also see presentations from staff about projects they are delivering in school.
How do we know we make a difference?
We consistently review the impact we are having on the school and keep the best interests of the children at the forefront of any conversation. Over the last year, we have made a positive impact on the support provided for subject leaders, reviewing and agreeing monitoring visits, hearing about the work taking place in school to develop the curriculum, questioning how school supports the well-being of staff and senior leaders, challenging the school about what led to the strong results last year, what it was based on and how it can be sustained for the future.
How could you get involved with the Local Governing Committee?
Our governor meetings are closed meetings. Governors generally hold their office for a period of four years and when parent governor positions become available, they will be advertised in the newsletter, along with application details. Following this, if you would like to join the governing committee, please leave a message with the school office and the appropriate person will get in contact with you. Please note that our parent governors are elected by Auriol parents and when a position is available, an election will be held.
